safety.title: Safety
safety.description: How Oomba Academy keeps kids safe: games in a locked box, every game checked, chat only with real-life friends.
safety.heading: How we keep Oomba Academy safe

box.h: Games are kept in a box
box.p1: Every game runs in a locked box (a sandbox). Games cannot reach the internet, cannot see your account, and cannot open other pages.

checked.p1: A robot checker reads every version of every game. Games for everyone also get a careful review before anyone else can play them.
checked.p2: If something slips through, tap 🚩 Report on the game page. When three people report a game, it is hidden until our team looks.

chat.p1: You can only chat with people you added using their secret friend code. Chat blocks bad words, phone numbers, emails, addresses and links.
chat.p2: You can block or report anyone, any time. Grown-ups can turn chat off on the Me page.

personal.p1: We never ask you for your email, age or address, or for your real name (your school may add it to its class list). Pick a fun made-up name.

ads.p1: There are no ads on Oomba Academy. Nothing is for sale, and nothing pops up over a game.
ads.paid1: There are no ads on Oomba Academy. Playing is always free. You never have to pay for anything here, and nothing pops up over a game.

parents.title: For grown-ups
parents.description: What Oomba Academy is, what data it keeps, how friends and chat work, and how the AI Builder stays kid-safe.
parents.heading: For grown-ups

what.p1: A free website where kids play web games and build their own by describing them to an AI Builder. No downloads, no purchases, no loot boxes, no in-game money that costs money.
what.paid1: A website where kids play web games and build their own by describing them to an AI Builder. Playing is free, and so is a daily allowance of Builder messages. Families and schools can buy extra Builder messages. There are no in-game purchases, no loot boxes and no in-game money that costs money.

plans.p1: Free to build, with extra Builder messages for families and schools.
plans.p2: Plans and payments are covered by our Terms of Service, our Refund and Cancellation Policy and our Privacy Policy.

stored.p1: Own accounts keep a made-up name, a password (stored scrambled) and what your child does here: the games they make, their chats with the Builder and any pictures or files they add, saves, scores, ratings, favorites, friends, chat messages, a profile photo if they upload one, and settings such as language and theme. Guest play keeps a made-up name, saves, scores, ratings and favorites.
stored.p2: A school account is one your child signs in to with a login card from school. It is made and owned by the school, and keeps the same things plus the student's real name as the school typed it for the class list (only the school's staff and our team see it), their classes, lesson progress, written answers and their teacher's feedback. If your child joins a class with their own account and a class code, the school keeps the same things for that class, including their real name if the teacher types one.
stored.paid3: Family plans never see class activity: a grown-up linked to a student sees only that student's family extra messages.
stored.p4: Their Oomba character: own accounts can design a drawn character that games use as the hero (a body shape, skin tone, hair, eyes, clothes and colours chosen from our lists). It is kept with their account as those choices only, never a photo or a picture of them, and it is deleted with the account.

never.p1: We never ask for an email address, age, home address, location or payment details, and there is nothing to buy. Hidden location data is removed from photos and pictures before they are kept. There are no ads, and no advertising or tracking cookies.
never.paid1: We never ask children for an email address, age, home address, location or payment details, and children are never asked to pay. A grown-up can choose a plan, and payment goes through Stripe; we never see card numbers. Hidden location data is removed from photos and pictures before they are kept. There are no ads, and no advertising or tracking cookies.

ai.p1: To make a game, the messages, pictures and files your child gives the Builder are sent to Claude, an AI made by the company Anthropic, which writes the game. Your child's name and username are not sent with them. Profile photos are also sent to Claude to be checked before anyone sees them. Claude reviews games before they can be shared with everyone, and our team checks any it is unsure about. Chats between friends and lesson answers are not sent to the AI.
ai.p2: Speaking instead of typing: when your child taps the microphone in the Builder chat, the recording is sent to {provider}, a speech-to-text service, which turns it into words. Your child sees the words and can change them before sending. The recording is used only for this and deleted straight away: we never store it, and {provider} is not allowed to keep it or use it to train its systems. The words go through the same safety checks as a typed message.
ai.p3: Looking up facts: to get a game right, the Builder can look up a fact on the web (for example how fast a cheetah runs). Your child never sees the web pages or links. The Builder is told never to search for anything personal; if a search still looks personal, its results are not used and its words are not kept. Adult, gambling, social media and video sites are blocked. We keep a list of the searches, without your child's name or username, together with the game they were for, for 90 days so our team can check them.
ai.p4: AI voices: our own games, games made in the Builder, lesson quizzes and Oomba Live quizzes can read their words aloud with a computer-made voice from {ttsProvider}. Only fixed text is sent: text written by us or your child's teacher, and the lines written into a game when it was made. In a game a child made with the Builder, those lines can include words the child asked for; they are sent only when our safety check has passed that version of the game. What a player types or says while playing is never sent, and never their name. Your child is told the voices are made by AI, and can switch to the device's own voice with the 🔊 AI voices button.

keep.p1: We keep an account's data for as long as the account exists. None of it is deleted on a timer yet. A game your child deletes is taken off the site for everyone, but a copy stays on our server.
keep.p2: There is no button yet to delete an account or download its data. To ask for either, a grown-up can contact us. For a school account, ask the school; it can ask us.
keep.madeP2: There is no button yet to delete an account or download its data, except that a grown-up who made their child's account can delete it from their family page. To ask for a deletion or a copy of the data, a grown-up can contact us. For a school account, ask the school; it can ask us.
keep.paid1: We keep an account's own data for as long as the account exists, and none of it is deleted on a timer yet. A game your child deletes is taken off the site for everyone, but a copy stays on our server. Family links, link codes and billing records have their own timers: see how long we keep billing information.

friends.p1: Friends are added only by a 6-character friend code, never by searching names. Chat is text between accepted friends only, filtered for bad language and personal details, rate-limited, and reportable. You can switch chat off on the Me page.

builder.p1: The Builder follows fixed kid-safety rules: no gore, no horror jump-scares, no gambling, no real brands or real people, no chat or data collection inside games, no links out. Requests that break the rules are kindly refused.

languages.p1: Pick a language with the 🌐 button at the top of any page or on the Me page. The Builder answers in that language and writes the words inside new games in it too. The same safety filters check every message, in every language.

families.p1: A parent or guardian can make their own grown-up account and link it to their child's account. Your child has to say yes on their own page.

made.h: If you make your child's account
made.p1: On your family page you can make your child's own account instead of linking one they already have. Your child signs in with the made-up name and password you choose.
made.li1: It is your child's account. Please don't chat or play as them: friends think they are talking to your child.
made.li2: You see counts only (games, uploads, saves, scores, friends, chat messages sent, which browsers are signed in), up to yesterday. Never what your child made, wrote or said.
made.li3: Your child is told that a grown-up made the account and what you can see. They can unlink or report you on their Me page, and then pick a new password.
made.li4: Before you make it, you read what the account keeps and tick that you are the child's parent or legal guardian. That, and paying for a plan, is not a parental consent check under children's privacy laws.
made.li5: You can change the password, see what we keep and delete the account from your family page. We keep it until you delete it: there are no automatic deletion timers yet.

live.p1: Teachers and grown-ups can run a live game for a class or a group: everyone joins with a short code from the host's screen and plays at the same time.
live.p2: Players never type anything, and there is no chat. A player without an account gets a made-up name from a fixed list of kind animal names and a random character. They need no account, and we set no cookie for them.
live.p3: We keep nothing about guests after the game ends. In a teacher's own class, students' scores go into the class gradebook, like any other class work. Codes stop working when the game ends.
live.p4: Every player can report a game with one tap, and the host can remove a player or lock the room.

sdk.title: For builders
sdk.description: The small helper every Oomba Academy game gets: saving, scores, effects, sounds and the player's language.
sdk.heading: Game SDK

brb.p1: Every game gets a small helper called BRB. {get} and {set} save progress for each player. localStorage also works and is saved to the cloud.
brb.p2: {submit} adds to the leaderboard (best score only). {over} ends a round.
brb.p5: {lang} is the player's language (like "fr" or "ar") and {dir} is "rtl" for right-to-left languages, so a game can speak the player's language.

rules.p1: Games cannot use the internet, cookies, forms, pop-ups or links. Fonts from Google Fonts and libraries from cdnjs are allowed. Keep each game under 2 MB.

legal.notYet: Paid plans are not on sale yet. The parts of this page about them apply once they are.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.description: The rules for using Oomba Academy: accounts, safety rules, games you make, paid plans and billing.
terms.heading: Terms of Service

who.h: 1. Who we are and what these terms cover
who.p1: Oomba Academy (oomba.ai) is an educational website where kids aged 8 to 14, their families and their teachers play web games and build their own games with an AI "Builder".
who.p2: The service is run by Oomba Academy ("Oomba Academy", "we", "us"). You can reach us at {email}.
who.p3: These terms are the rules for using the site. They apply to everyone who uses it. Our Privacy Policy and our Refund and Cancellation Policy are part of these terms.
who.p4: A note for kids: these terms are written for grown-ups. The short version for you is on the Safety page: be kind, keep personal details private, only build games that follow the Builder's rules, and tell a grown-up you trust if anything worries you.

accounts.li1: Guest: for anyone who wants to play. Made with one tap on a game. Keeps a made-up name, saves, scores, ratings and favorites.
accounts.li2: Own account: for a child (or anyone) who wants to build, keep games and add friends. Made on the site with a made-up username and a password.
accounts.li3: School account: for a student in a school that uses Oomba Academy. Made and owned by the school. The student signs in with a login card (or, if the school turns it on, a school Google account).
accounts.li4: Teacher and school admin: for school staff. Set up by the school or by us.
accounts.li5: Grown-up account: for a parent or legal guardian who wants to link to their child's account or buy a Family plan. Made with a name and a password of at least 12 characters.
accounts.p1: Oomba Academy is made for children aged 8 to 14.
accounts.li6: If you are under 18, a parent or legal guardian must agree to these terms for you, and they are responsible for how you use the site. Paying for a plan is not how a parent gives permission for a child's account (see section 7.9).
accounts.li7: A school account is created by the school. The school is responsible for having the right to create it and for telling parents about it (see section 3).
accounts.li8: You must be 18 or older and the parent or legal guardian of every child you link to. When you sign up you confirm this with a checkbox. We do not check it, so please be honest: linking to a child who is not yours breaks these terms, and we will end the link and may close your account.
accounts.li9: A grown-up account can play games and build games with the Builder. Its games go through the same safety checks as every game. It can connect with other grown-up accounts only. It cannot chat, add kids as friends, post, or have a public profile, and its games never show which children are linked to it.
accounts.li10: Keep your password private. You are responsible for what happens in your grown-up account, including purchases.
accounts.li11: To protect against a child buying something on a shared device, we ask for your password again before you start or change a plan.
accounts.s4: Linking a grown-up to a child
accounts.li16: The child gets a short code on their own Me page. It works once, for 24 hours.
accounts.li13: You enter the code on your family page.
accounts.li14: The child must say Yes on their own page. They can also say No or Report.
accounts.li15: The child can Unlink or Report at any time. A report ends the link at once and goes to our team.
accounts.p2: A linked grown-up sees the child's username and display name, and how many of the family's extra Builder messages the child used yesterday and this month. A linked grown-up does not see the child's chats, friends, games, live activity or anything about their school.
accounts.p3: School accounts cannot be linked to a grown-up account.

schools.p1: If you use Oomba Academy for a school, these terms apply to the school, its staff and its students, together with any written agreement we sign with the school (for example a student data privacy agreement). If the two conflict, the signed agreement wins.
schools.li1: confirms it has the authority to accept these terms and to create accounts for its students;
schools.li2: is responsible for telling parents about its use of Oomba Academy, and for any consent it needs from them under laws such as COPPA, FERPA and state student-privacy laws;
schools.li3: owns its class lists and student records. We use them only to run the service for the school.
schools.p3: Only school admins see the school's billing. Teachers and students never see prices.

rules.h: 4. Using Oomba Academy safely: the rules
rules.p1: These rules apply to everyone, including what you type into the Builder, the games you make, chat messages, pictures you upload and your profile.
rules.li1: share personal details (yours or anyone else's): real full names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, school names in public places, or social media handles;
rules.li2: bully, threaten, harass or be mean to anyone;
rules.li3: make or share anything with gore, horror jump-scares, adult content, hate, gambling, drugs, or real weapons used to hurt people;
rules.li4: use real brands, real people, or other people's characters, music or art you don't have the right to use;
rules.li5: try to get around the safety filters, the Builder's rules, the game sandbox, or the message limits (for example with many accounts);
rules.li6: make games that collect data, chat, or link out of the site;
rules.li7: try to break, overload, scrape or attack the site, or get into accounts that are not yours;
rules.li8: buy or try to buy a plan with a payment card you are not allowed to use.
rules.li9: Every Builder message is screened before the AI sees it. Messages that break the rules are kindly refused.
rules.li10: A robot checker reads every version of every game. Games shared with everyone also get a careful review by an AI model, and a person on our team checks any game it is unsure about. Games shared with a class or school are checked before they reach that audience.
rules.li11: Chat is text only, only between friends who added each other by friend code, and filtered for bad language and personal details.
rules.li12: Anyone signed in can report a game. When three people report a game, it is hidden until our team looks. Anyone can block or report a chat partner.
rules.li13: Our team can approve, reject, hide or take down games, and pause, suspend or ban accounts. We log every moderation action.
rules.p2: No checking is perfect. If you see something wrong, please report it or email {email}.

ai.li1: The Builder uses Claude, an AI made by Anthropic, to write games from what you describe. What the AI makes can be wrong, buggy, or unexpectedly similar to something that already exists.
ai.li2: We check games before they are shared widely (section 4), but we do not promise that every game is free of mistakes.
ai.li3: Do not rely on games or AI answers for anything important (health, safety, money, homework answers you have not checked).
ai.li4: What you send to the Builder (messages, pictures, files) is sent to Anthropic to make the game. See our Privacy Policy for details.

games.h: 6. Games you make: who owns them
games.p1: You (or, for a school account, you and your school as the school's policies say) keep whatever rights you have in the games you make here: your ideas, your words, your pictures and your designs.
games.p2: Some parts of a game are not yours alone:
games.li1: the game engine, the site's sound effects, the starter templates, the Three.js library and other building blocks belong to us or our licensors;
games.li2: parts written by the AI may not be protected by copyright at all.
games.p3: So we can run the site, you give Oomba Academy a worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to store, copy, run, show, take screenshots of, check (with people and AI tools, including sending the game to Anthropic for review), and make small technical changes to (for example to fit a screen or fix a safety problem) the games, pictures and text you put on the site, only to run, protect and improve Oomba Academy and only to show them to the people you chose (only me, friends, your classes, your school, or everyone).
games.li3: This licence ends when you delete the game, except that: a deleted game is taken off the site for everyone, but a copy stays on our server so reports and safety records still point to something; we may keep backup copies for a limited time; and games other people already saved scores in keep those scores.
games.li4: We will not sell your games or use them in ads, and we don't use them in our marketing without asking.
games.li5: Other players can play games you share with them. They do not get the right to copy or remix them. If remixing is ever added, we will update these terms first.
games.p4: Only upload or describe things you have the right to use. If you think something on Oomba Academy copies your work, email {email} with what it is and where it is. We take down infringing material and close the accounts of people who do it again and again.

plans.s1: 7.1 What is free and what you pay for
plans.li1: Playing is free for everyone, and so is a free daily allowance of Builder messages.
plans.li2: Paid plans only add more Builder messages. Paying never unlocks a feature that free users don't have.
plans.li3: Children never see prices or plans, and are never asked to pay. Only grown-up accounts and school admins can buy a plan.
plans.li4: We can change the size of the free allowance at any time. We will announce a change on the For grown-ups page before it applies.
plans.li5: Bought by a grown-up account for up to 4 linked children (each child must have confirmed the link).
plans.li6: Monthly or yearly, at the price shown to the grown-up before they buy.
plans.li7: It gives the family a set number of extra Builder messages each month, shared by the linked children, on top of each child's free daily messages. The number is shown before you buy and on your family page afterwards.
plans.li8: Each child uses their free daily messages first; extras are used after that, or when the free Builder is resting.
plans.li9: Extras reset at the start of each calendar month (UTC) and do not roll over. A "Pro quality" message counts as 2. A message that fails to build is given back.
plans.li10: To stop one child using the whole month in a day, there is a limit on how many extra messages one child can use in a day, and a limit on unusually expensive use.
plans.li11: A child in a school with a paid School plan builds from the school's allowance in class, never from the family's extras.
plans.li12: Family plans are for US families for now. You need a US billing address and a US payment card (or Apple Pay or Google Pay).
plans.li13: The Teacher plan is priced per teacher per year, with no charge per student. It covers all of that teacher's classes and students. It starts with a 14-day free trial that needs no card. If no card is added by the end of the trial, the plan simply stops. Each teacher, email address and school can have one free trial.
plans.li14: A teacher with the plan and the students in their classes share a daily number of Builder messages, shown before you start and on the teacher's My classes page. When they run out, everyone uses the free allowance until the next day (UTC).
plans.li15: Schools buy Teacher plans at the same price per teacher and give them to their teachers on the school's Billing tab. Added teachers are billed straight away for the rest of the year; fewer teachers take effect at renewal. A school that bought a plan priced per student before keeps that plan, at its price, when it renews.
plans.li16: Paying: by card online, or by invoice (a purchase order is fine). Invoices are due 30 days after they are sent (net 30) and can be paid by card, bank transfer or ACH, or by check (email us for the mailing address).
plans.li17: Tax-exempt schools can send us their exemption certificate.
plans.li18: Payments are processed by Stripe. You pay on Stripe's own page. We never see or store your card number.
plans.li19: Prices are in US dollars and don't include sales tax. Where the law requires it, tax is added at checkout or on the invoice.
plans.li20: Stripe sends your receipts. The charge shows on your statement as OOMBA ACADEMY.
plans.li21: A monthly Family plan renews every month, and a yearly plan every year, at the price then in effect (see 7.7), charged to the payment method on file.
plans.li22: Before you pay, the checkout page shows the price, how often you'll be charged, and that it renews until you cancel. By paying, you agree to the automatic renewal.
plans.li23: We send a reminder before a yearly plan renews.
plans.li24: School invoice plans renew each year with a new invoice. The school's Billing tab shows a reminder 30 days before.
plans.li25: Cancel anytime online: on your family page, choose Manage billing, then cancel on Stripe's page. Schools: Manage billing on the Billing tab, or email us.
plans.li26: Cancelling stops the next renewal. The plan keeps working until the end of the period you paid for, then your family or school goes back to the free allowance.
plans.li27: Nothing is deleted when a plan ends.
plans.li28: Refunds are covered by our Refund and Cancellation Policy: in short, a full refund if you ask within 14 days of the payment that starts a plan or of a yearly renewal. Monthly renewals are not refunded, and there are no partial refunds otherwise.
plans.li29: We may change prices or what a plan includes. We will tell you before the change applies to you, by a notice on your family page (or the school's Billing tab) and by email to the address you gave Stripe, at least 7 and no more than 30 days before the renewal it applies to.
plans.li30: A new price applies from your next renewal, never to a period you already paid for. If you don't want the new price, cancel before that renewal.
plans.li31: We won't reduce the number of extra messages in a period you have already paid for.
plans.li32: Card payments: if a payment fails, the plan keeps working for 7 days while the payment is retried. Please update your card on your family page. If it still hasn't gone through, the plan ends.
plans.li33: Invoices: if an invoice isn't paid, the plan keeps working until 30 days after the due date. Then the plan ends.
plans.li34: When a plan ends this way, the family or school simply goes back to the free allowance. Nothing is deleted or locked, and school classes keep working.
plans.li35: If a payment is disputed with the bank (a chargeback) or the bank warns it may be fraud, we end the plan right away so the card is not charged again. Please email us if this was a mistake.
plans.p2: Buying a plan does not change what we do with a child's data or what a parent has agreed to about it. How parents are told about their child's use of Oomba Academy is a separate matter, covered in our Privacy Policy.

ending.li1: You can stop using Oomba Academy at any time. There is no delete button yet: to delete an account or get a copy of its data, email {email} (school accounts: ask the school, which can ask us). If a grown-up account with a plan is deleted, we cancel the plan first.
ending.madeLi1: You can stop using Oomba Academy at any time. A grown-up who made their child's account can delete it from their family page. Otherwise there is no delete button yet: to delete an account or get a copy of its data, email {email} (school accounts: ask the school, which can ask us). If a grown-up account with a plan is deleted, we cancel the plan first.
ending.li2: We may pause, limit or close an account, take down a game, or end a family link if someone breaks these terms, puts a child at risk, or if the law requires it. We'll explain why when we can, unless that would put someone at risk.
ending.li3: If a child's account is suspended, the family plan keeps working for the other linked children. A suspension alone is not a reason for a refund.
ending.li4: If we close a grown-up account for fraud or serious misuse, the plan ends and is not refunded, unless the law requires it.
ending.li5: If we end a paid plan for a reason that is not your fault, or we shut down Oomba Academy, we refund the unused part of the period you paid for.

disclaimers.p1: We work hard to make Oomba Academy safe, fun and available, but:
disclaimers.li1: the site and the Builder are provided "as is" and "as available". They may sometimes be down, slow or changed. The Builder can "rest" when our safety spending limits are reached or our AI provider is unavailable, and in rare cases this can affect paid plans too;
disclaimers.li2: we don't promise that games (ours, AI-made or made by other players) are free of mistakes;
disclaimers.li3: to the extent the law allows, we disclaim implied warranties such as merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose and non-infringement.
disclaimers.p2: Some states don't allow some of these disclaimers, so they may not apply to you. Nothing here takes away rights you have under consumer law that can't be waived.

liability.p1: To the extent the law allows:
liability.li1: we are not liable for indirect, incidental, special or consequential losses (for example lost data you didn't save elsewhere);
liability.li2: our total liability for any claim about Oomba Academy is limited to the greater of what you paid us in the 12 months before the claim, or 100 US dollars.
liability.p2: These limits do not apply to liability that can't be limited by law, including for our gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud, or personal injury caused by our negligence.

disputes.li1: Talk to us first. Most problems can be fixed by email. Please write to {email} and give us 30 days to try to sort it out.
disputes.li2: These terms are governed by the laws of the US state where Oomba Academy is based and by US federal law, without regard to conflict-of-laws rules.
disputes.li3: Disputes go to the state or federal courts where Oomba Academy is based, or to small-claims court where you live if your claim qualifies.
disputes.li4: If you live in a state whose consumer-protection law gives you rights that these terms can't take away, you keep them.

changes.li1: We may update these terms. We'll change the "Last updated" date.
changes.li2: For important changes we will give notice at least 30 days before they apply: on the For grown-ups page, on the family page and the school Billing tab, and by email to paying grown-ups and school billing contacts.
changes.li3: Changes don't apply to a dispute that started before the change.
changes.li4: If you don't agree to a change, you can stop using the site and cancel your plan before it applies. Continuing after that means you accept the new terms.

other.li1: If a court finds part of these terms can't be enforced, the rest still applies.
other.li2: If we don't enforce a rule right away, we haven't given up the right to do so later.
other.li3: You may not transfer your account or these terms to someone else. We may transfer them if Oomba Academy is sold or reorganized, and we will tell you.
other.li4: These terms, our Privacy Policy and our Refund and Cancellation Policy are the whole agreement between you and us about the site (plus any signed school agreement, section 3).

refunds.title: Refunds and cancelling
refunds.description: How to cancel an Oomba Academy Family or School plan, and when you can get your money back.
refunds.heading: Refund and Cancellation Policy

intro.p1: This page explains how to cancel an Oomba Academy plan and when you can get your money back. It is part of our Terms of Service.
intro.p2: Playing and the free daily Builder messages are always free. This policy is only about the paid Family, Teacher and School plans, which add more Builder messages.
intro.p3: Spark Packs, one-time top-ups of Builder messages for a family with a plan, have their own section below.

cancel.li1: Cancel anytime. There is no cancellation fee.
cancel.li2: Families: sign in to your grown-up account, open your family page, choose Manage billing, then cancel on Stripe's page. We ask for your password first.
cancel.li3: Schools: a school admin opens the school's Billing tab and chooses Manage billing, or emails {email} (invoice schools).
cancel.li4: When it takes effect: at the end of the month or year you already paid for. Until then the plan keeps working. After that, your family or school goes back to the free allowance.
cancel.li5: Nothing is deleted. Games, saves and classes stay exactly as they are.

refunds.p1: Full refund within 14 days. If you ask within 14 days of the payment that starts a plan, or of a yearly renewal, we refund that payment in full, including any tax charged.
refunds.p2: Monthly renewals are not refunded. You can cancel a monthly plan at any time so the next renewal doesn't happen.
refunds.p3: Otherwise, no partial refunds. If you cancel later, the plan simply runs to the end of the period you paid for. We don't refund unused days or unused messages.
refunds.p4: What a refund does: a refund ends the plan straight away (we cancel it first, then refund), so the extra messages stop at once.
refunds.p5: How to ask: email {email} from any address. Tell us the name of your grown-up account (or school), and the date and amount from your Stripe receipt. We'll reply within 3 business days.
refunds.p6: When you get the money: the refund goes back to the card or account you paid with. Banks usually take 5 to 10 business days to show it.
refunds.p7: Schools paying by invoice: the 14 days start on the date the payment reaches us. Paid by check? We refund by check or bank transfer.
refunds.p8: Free trials: a Teacher plan's free trial costs nothing, and ends by itself if no card is added. If you add a card, the first payment is taken when the trial ends, and the 14 days start then.

sparks.p1: A Spark Pack is one payment for extra Builder messages, for a family with a Basic or Family plan. It doesn't renew, so there is nothing to cancel.
sparks.li1: Unused pack, within 14 days: if you ask within 14 days of buying a pack and none of its messages have been used, we refund it in full. Ask the same way as for a plan (see How to ask above).
sparks.li2: Otherwise, packs are not refunded: once some of a pack's messages are used, or after 14 days, we don't refund it, unless the law where you live says we must.
sparks.li3: What a refund does: as soon as the refund goes through, the messages left in the pack are taken back. A full refund ends the pack; a partial refund takes back that share of its messages. Messages already used stay used.
sparks.li4: When packs end: a pack's messages end one year after you buy it. A pack keeps working after your plan ends, until then. Messages left when a pack ends are not refunded.
sparks.li5: Disputed the charge with your bank? The pack ends straight away, like a plan.

special.li1: Paid twice by mistake? If two plans start for the same family or school, we cancel the extra one and refund it automatically.
special.li2: Payment didn't go through? Cards: the plan keeps working for 7 days while the payment is retried. Invoices: until 30 days after the due date. After that the plan ends and you're back on the free allowance. Nothing is deleted.
special.li3: A child used your card without asking? Email us right away. We will cancel the plan and, if you ask within 14 days of the payment, refund it in full.
special.li4: Disputed the charge with your bank? We end the plan straight away so the card isn't charged again. Please email us first; we can usually fix it faster.
special.li5: If we end your plan for a reason that isn't your fault, or we close Oomba Academy, we refund the unused part of the period you paid for.
special.li6: We may give a refund in other cases if we choose. Doing so once doesn't mean we must do it again.

rights.p1: This policy doesn't take away any refund rights you have under the law where you live.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.description: What Oomba Academy keeps, what it never collects, what the AI sees, and how grown-up accounts, payments and school billing work.
privacy.heading: Privacy Policy

intro.p1: This policy explains what Oomba Academy (oomba.ai, "we", "us") keeps about the people who use it, what we never collect, and how grown-up accounts, family links, payments and school billing work. The same facts about children's accounts are on the For grown-ups page. Questions: {email}.

grownups.li1: the name you type when you sign up (it can be a first name or nickname; children never see it: they see only "your grown-up");
grownups.li2: your password, stored scrambled (we can't read it);
grownups.li8: if you sign up or sign in with Google: your Google account's id and email address, to sign you in and to send account emails, such as a password reset or trial emails (never the Google photo);
grownups.li3: that you ticked "I am a parent or guardian, 18 or older" (we don't check this);
grownups.li4: your sign-in sessions, including your browser's name (user agent), and when you last re-entered your password for a billing step;
grownups.li5: which children you linked, when, and whether a link is pending, linked or ended;
grownups.li6: your plan: Stripe's customer and subscription numbers, plan type, monthly or yearly, status, seats, dates and amounts;
grownups.li7: a record of important actions (for example "plan started", "child linked", "refund"). These records never contain card details or email addresses.
grownups.p1: What we don't ask for: your phone number, home address or age, and no email unless you sign up or sign in with Google. (Stripe asks for some of these when you pay: see Payments below.)
grownups.p2: A grown-up account can build games. They go through the same safety checks as every game, and a game shared with everyone shows the grown-up’s display name and “Grown-up builder”. A grown-up account can connect with other grown-up accounts only; it can’t chat, add kids as friends or have a public profile, and doesn’t appear in search. We never show publicly which children are linked to a grown-up, or their names.

linking.li7: The code: your child gets a short code on their Me page. We store it scrambled. It works once, for 24 hours.
linking.li2: The child says yes: the link only starts when your child confirms it on their own page. They can say No, or Report it to our team. Reports are kept while open and deleted 1 year after we close them.
linking.li3: What you see about your child: their username and display name, how many of the family's extra Builder messages they used yesterday and so far this month, and whether they are building on the Family plan or the free allowance.
linking.li4: What you don't see: today's live activity (so you can't tell when they're online), their chats, friends or games, any messages charged to a school, or whether they are in a school at all.
linking.li5: What your child sees about you: only the words "your grown-up", never the name you typed.
linking.li6: Counting messages: to count the family's extras, we record for each Builder message which allowance paid for it (free, family or school), how many messages it counted as, and its AI cost.

payments.p1: Payments are handled by Stripe, Inc. You pay on Stripe's own page, not on ours. Stripe's privacy policy is at stripe.com/privacy.
payments.p2: What Stripe collects from you (on Stripe's pages):
payments.li1: your email address (Stripe sends receipts, failed-payment notices and renewal reminders to it);
payments.li2: your card details, or your Apple Pay or Google Pay wallet;
payments.li3: your billing address (needed for sales tax and to check that family plans are for US families);
payments.li4: information Stripe uses to prevent fraud, such as details about your device and connection.
payments.p3: What we send to Stripe for a family plan: a random family number so we can match the payment to your plan. We do not send Stripe your name, your child's name or username, or anything about how your child uses the site. For schools, see School billing below.
payments.p4: What we get back and keep: Stripe's customer and subscription numbers, the plan, status (active, past due, cancelled), dates, amounts, seat count, and whether a payment was paid, failed, refunded or disputed.
payments.p5: What we never see or keep: your full card number or security code. For a family plan, our own database does not store your email or billing address. Stripe's messages to our server can include them, but we don't save them. A school's invoice request is different: see School billing below.
payments.p6: Who on our side can see more: the owner can see your email, billing address, receipts and the last 4 digits of your card in Stripe's dashboard. We use them only to run your plan: to answer your questions, give refunds, and tell you about important changes to your plan, price or our terms. The site has no email system of its own, so these notices are sent from {email} to the email Stripe holds. We never use it for marketing.
payments.p7: Fraud and disputes: if your bank reports a payment as disputed or likely fraud, Stripe tells us. We end the plan and keep a record of what happened.
payments.p8: Sales tax: Stripe calculates sales tax from your billing address where we are required to collect it.
payments.p9: Cookies: our site adds no new cookies for payments. Stripe's pages are run by Stripe and follow Stripe's policy.

schoolBilling.li1: Who sees it: only the school's admins and our team. Teachers and students never see billing.
schoolBilling.li2: What we keep when a school asks for an invoice: the number of seats, purchase order number, the billing contact's name and email, the school's billing address, whether the school says it is tax-exempt, and any note.
schoolBilling.li3: What goes to Stripe: when we create the school's invoices, the school's name, the billing contact's email, the billing address and the purchase order number are saved with Stripe, which sends the invoices. The contact's name, the note and the tax-exempt answer stay only with us. Nothing is sent until we create the invoices. A school that pays by card types its name and billing address on Stripe's page instead.
schoolBilling.li4: How long: the contact's name and email, the address, the note and the purchase order number in our database are deleted 2 years after the request is closed. Stripe keeps the school's address and purchase order number with its invoices (see below).
schoolBilling.li5: Seats are counted in teachers: the school admins choose which teachers have one. Billing does not use students' names or work.
schoolBilling.li6: Families never see class activity: a grown-up linked to a student sees only that student's family extra messages.
schoolBilling.li7: Asking for a School plan: a teacher can ask their school's admins for a School plan. We keep which teacher asked, for which school and when, never a message. The school's admins see who asked until they dismiss it or the school gets a plan, and we delete it 90 days after that. Teachers only see whether their school has a plan.

schoolSetup.li1: What we keep when a teacher or school leader asks us to set up a school (the form on our teachers page): the school's name, their role, their work email, about how many students, the country, the language of the page and when it was sent. If they were signed in to a grown-up or school staff account, we also keep which account sent it. A guest's account is never kept with a request. If they made their teacher account with the form, we also keep the work email with that account.
schoolSetup.li5: When a teacher creates their school while signing up and types a work email, we keep the school's name, their name, that email, the language of the page, when it was sent and their account, for the same uses and for as long as a request. The email is also kept with their account.
schoolSetup.li2: What we use it for: to set up the school, to reply to the request, to send the school's welcome guide, and to send a password-reset link if the account's owner asks for one. We don't send newsletters, and we don't share it with Stripe or anyone else.
schoolSetup.li4: How long: deleted 1 year after we close the request (or 1 year after it was sent, if it is never closed).

children.p1: Children never see prices, plans or a "buy" button, and are never asked to pay or to ask a grown-up to pay.
children.p2: Paying is not how we ask a parent for permission. Buying a plan doesn't change what we collect about a child, what we use it for, or what a parent has agreed to.
children.p3: Your rights as a parent (own accounts): you can ask us to show you what we keep about your child, to delete it, or to stop collecting more. Email {email}. There is no delete or download button yet, so we handle these requests by hand, and we will need to check that you are the parent before we act. Unlinking or cancelling a plan does not delete your child's account.
children.p4: School accounts: a school account is made and owned by the school. For those accounts we act on the school's behalf and under its direction: we use student information only to provide Oomba Academy to the school, never for advertising, and we don't sell it. Parents of school accounts should ask the school to see or delete records; the school can ask us. A data agreement the school has signed with us comes first.
children.p5: No selling, no ads: we don't sell anyone's personal information, show ads, or use advertising or tracking cookies.
children.p6: AI voices: when a game, lesson or Oomba Live reads text aloud with an AI voice, only that text is sent from our server to {ttsProvider} to make the sound, with nothing that says who is playing or who made the game. It is always fixed text: written by us or a teacher, or a line written into a game when it was made. In a game a child made with the Builder, those lines can include words the child asked for; a line is sent only if that version of the game passed our safety check, and never if it has rude words, an email address, a phone number or the player's own name in it. What a player types or says while playing is never sent. {ttsProvider} may keep the text for a limited time to check for misuse. Players are told these voices are made by a computer.

billingKeep.h: How long we keep billing information
billingKeep.li1: Link codes: deleted 30 days after they are used or expire.
billingKeep.li2: Pending links: deleted when they expire (24 hours) or the child says No.
billingKeep.li3: Ended links: deleted 90 days after they end (a record with account numbers only stays in our action log).
billingKeep.li4: Link reports: kept while open, then 1 year after they are closed.
billingKeep.li5: Plan and payment records (Stripe numbers, amounts, dates) and Stripe's invoices: 7 years, for tax law, even after an account is deleted.
billingKeep.li6: School invoice requests' contact details, address, note and purchase order number: 2 years after the request is closed.
billingKeep.li7: Grown-up account, family and links: until you ask us to delete the account. We cancel any plan first.

where.p1: Family plans are for US families for now.

more.p1: Grown-up accounts, family links, payments, school billing and how long we keep billing records are explained in the full privacy policy for grown-ups and schools.

made.h: Accounts a grown-up makes for a child
made.p1: A parent or legal guardian with a grown-up account can make their child's own account on their family page. It is an ordinary child's account, with the same rules, limits and safety checks as any other.
made.li1: What it keeps: the same as any child's account: games, Builder chats, pictures and files uploaded, game saves, scores, ratings and likes, friends and friend chat, a profile photo if one is added, settings, and sign-in cookies with the browser's name.
made.li8: What the grown-up sees: how many extra Builder messages the child used (up to yesterday), and counts of games, Builder chats, uploads, saves, scores, friends and chat messages sent, whether there is a profile photo, and which browsers are signed in. Never the content. The counts stop at the end of yesterday, so nothing the child adds today shows before tomorrow, but something the child deletes or ends today (a game, a friend, a sign-in) can already be missing from them.
made.li3: The grown-up chose the username and password. We ask them not to use the child's real name, and we refuse names that look like a real name, a birth year or the grown-up's own name.
made.li4: The child is told that a grown-up made the account and what that grown-up can see. They can unlink or report the grown-up on their Me page; that asks them for a new password, so the grown-up can't sign in as them any more.
made.li5: Before making the account, the grown-up reads a notice about what we keep and ticks that they have read it and that they are the child's parent or legal guardian. We keep a record of that: when, and which version of the notice. This is not a parental consent check under children's privacy laws, and we don't treat it as one. Paying for a plan isn't one either.
made.li9: The grown-up can see these counts and delete the account from their family page: everything the child made, wrote and uploaded goes straight away. We keep a short record that the account existed and who made it, the old username is held back for 90 days so nobody else can take it, and a class the child used to be in keeps its own records. If the child is in a school class now, the teacher removes them from the class first.
made.li7: How long: as long as the account exists. We have no automatic deletion timers yet.

manip.p1: Live class sessions: when a teacher runs a live math manipulatives session, each student's board in it (their pieces, sticky notes, text and answers) is kept for their teacher and deleted 30 days after the session ends. Where students point (their cursors) and raised hands are not stored.
manip.p2: Drafting a board with AI: a teacher can describe a lesson and have the AI draft a board for it. Only the teacher's description is sent to our AI provider, Anthropic. Student work and names are never sent.

companion.p1: Teachers with the Teacher plan can chat with Oomba from a bubble on their own pages. Students and children never see it. A teacher's messages, the text of a document they attach and a picture they attach are sent to our AI provider, Anthropic, to make the answer. Before anything is sent, we take out the names of the teacher's students, emails, phone numbers and links. Pictures that show a person are refused and never kept. Each name becomes a placeholder like "[student 1]". Which student it stands for stays on our servers, so Oomba can give a point to the right student without the name ever being sent.
companion.p2: Oomba sees only what a teacher has open and safe facts about it (a class's grade and size, a dashboard's widgets, a Figures worksheet's questions, a manipulatives board's items and steps), never students' names, answers or work. It changes a dashboard only after the teacher taps Apply. On a Figures worksheet or a manipulatives board, it makes the change the teacher asks for right away, and the teacher can undo it. When a teacher asks, it can also give a dashboard point to a student or to the whole class, which the teacher can undo.
companion.p3: When web search is on, Oomba may send short searches to Anthropic's web search. They never include names or a location, sites for adults, gambling, social networks and the like are blocked, and every search is logged for our team without the teacher's name. Pages found on the web are shown as sources Oomba hasn't checked.
companion.p4: A teacher can speak instead of typing: the sound is streamed to {provider} to turn it into words as they speak, and the audio is never kept, by us or by them. The words go into the message box for the teacher to check.
companion.p5: We keep a teacher's chat, with the text of what they attached, for 60 days after it was last used (a school can choose from 7 to 365 days); a picture is deleted once Oomba has answered, and within a day at the latest. New chat keeps the old chat in the teacher's chat history, under the same rule; a teacher can delete any chat there, and every chat is deleted with the account. A school admin can turn Oomba or its web search off for the school.

storybook.p1: Teachers can make picture books in the Story Library with Oomba. A teacher's words for the book are sent to our AI provider, Anthropic, to write it. Before anything is sent, we take out the names of the teacher's students, emails, phone numbers and links. Students only read the finished books their teacher shares with their class; nothing a student does is sent.
storybook.p2: Book pictures: to draw a book's pictures, we send Google (the Gemini API) the book's own words about each picture (what happens, where, and how each made-up character looks), our picture style, and for a page the pictures of its characters drawn before. Never a student's name or work, the teacher's name or a class. Google may keep what we send for a limited time to check for misuse and does not use it to train its systems. Every picture is checked before it is shown; a picture that doesn't pass is not kept. The pictures are kept with the book and deleted with it.

promptTips.a: Say what kind of game first: “a racing game”, “a quiz”, “a platformer”. Then add the details.
promptTips.b: Tell the AI how you win and how you lose. Clear rules make a better game.
promptTips.c: Describe how it should look: colours, a theme like space or jungle, and who the hero is.
promptTips.d: Change one thing at a time. “Make the jump higher” works better than ten changes at once.
promptTips.e: Be specific. “Make the enemies slower in level 1” beats “make it easier”.
promptTips.f: Found a bug? Say what you did, what happened and what you expected to happen.
promptTips.g: Name the controls you want: arrow keys, tapping, swiping or the space bar.
promptTips.h: Ask for levels that get harder, like “3 levels, each one a bit faster”.
promptTips.i: Want sounds or a score? Ask for them: “add a coin sound and a high score”.
promptTips.j: Play your game after each change, then tell the AI exactly what to fix next.
promptTips.k: Give an example: “like a maze, but the walls move” helps the AI picture your idea.
promptTips.l: Not sure what to add? Ask the AI: “What are 3 ideas to make this more fun?”

learn.start: A round is each time the app asks the AI. It doesn’t remember, so the app sends it the chat again.
learn.look: This AI can read pictures, so it checks the screenshots for anything broken, blank or messy.
learn.scan: The safety program says exactly what was wrong, so the AI can fix just that part.
learn.retry: When a tool says something didn’t work, the AI reads why and tries another way.
learn.next: After each tool, the AI reads the result and picks the next step. That loop makes it an agent.
learn.thinking: Before it answers, this AI thinks quietly first, a bit like working something out in your head.
learn.long: Big ideas can take the AI a minute or two to plan before it writes any code. It keeps going even if you leave this page.
learn.msg: This AI reads new messages between steps, not in the middle of one. Then it can change its plan.
learn.auto: When the playtest finds a problem, the AI reads the report and fixes just that part. Then the app plays the game again.

write.learn: The AI writes code one small piece at a time, each time predicting what should come next.

facts.a: AI reads and writes in tokens, which are small pieces of words. A long word can be several tokens.
facts.b: An AI writes by predicting the next token, again and again, very fast.
facts.c: Ask the same thing twice and you may get a different answer, because the AI picks from likely next words.
facts.d: Every round, the AI reads the recent chat again. That’s why long chats use more tokens.
facts.e: An agent is an AI that uses tools in a loop. This Builder can take up to 20 rounds for each build.
facts.f: The Builder AI can’t use the internet. It builds from what it learned and what you tell it.
facts.g: AI models learn patterns from huge amounts of writing and code made by people.
facts.h: AI can sound sure and still be wrong. That’s why a safety program checks the code too.
facts.i: This Builder uses a big AI that thinks before it writes: slower, but better at tricky games.
facts.j: Always play your game yourself. Even clever AI misses things a real player would notice.
facts.k: You can send new ideas while the AI works. It reads them between its steps.

setup.title: Sign in with Google for schools
setup.heading: Sign in with Google for schools

what.p1: Students and staff can sign in to Oomba Academy with their school Google account, for example on a Chromebook. Oomba Academy only asks Google for basic sign-in information: the account's name and email address.

turnOn.h: Turn it on for your school
turnOn.p1: A school admin adds the school's Google Workspace domain on the school's Settings tab. Until then, nobody at the school can use Google sign-in.

trust.p1: Google lets students who are under 18 use an app only after the school's Google admin allows it. Otherwise they see “Access blocked”. Your Google admin can allow Oomba Academy like this (menu names may differ slightly):

setup.step1: Sign in to the Google Admin console (admin.google.com) as an admin.
setup.step2: Go to Security → Access and data control → API controls → Manage third-party app access.
setup.step3: Add an app, and search for this client ID: {id}
setup.step4: Pick the organisational units with students (and staff), choose Trusted or Limited, and save.
setup.step5: Or: for users under 18, allow apps that only ask for the basic information needed for Sign in with Google.
setup.step6: It can take a little while to apply. Then ask a student to try “Sign in with Google” again.

invite.p1: On a class's Students tab, paste the students' school email addresses. When a student signs in with that Google account, they join the class. Nothing is emailed.
invite.p2: Or turn on “join with Google” next to the class code: students with a school Google account type the code and join at once.

privacy.p1: We keep the Google account's id, email address and school domain while it is connected, to recognise it at sign-in. We never store the Google photo, never show a student's Google name on the game site, and never use the account to read anything else from Google.
privacy.p1c: We keep the Google account's id, email address and school domain while it is connected, to recognise it at sign-in. We never store the Google photo, never show a student's Google name on the game site, and read nothing else from a Google account unless a teacher connects Google Classroom.
privacy.classroom: When a teacher connects Google Classroom, we read only the names of the classes they teach and, for the class they link, each student's Google account id and name, to add them to the matching Oomba Academy class. We send Google only what the teacher asks for: an assignment (the lesson's title, a link to it and its due date) and each student's lesson score out of 100. We never send students' answers, feedback, games or drawings. The teacher's connection is stored encrypted until they disconnect or delete their account; disconnecting also revokes it at Google.
privacy.limitedUse: Oomba Academy's use and transfer of information received from Google APIs adheres to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements. We never sell this information, use it for advertising, or use it to train AI models, and our team looks at it only when needed for support, security or the law.
privacy.adults: Parents and teachers can also sign up with Google, with a personal or a school Google account. We keep that account's id and email address while it is connected, to sign them in and to send account emails, such as a password reset or trial emails. An email never joins two accounts on its own. Children never sign up with Google.

how.p1: Make a grown-up account: a name and a password of at least 12 characters. No email needed.
how.p2: Your child signs in, opens Me, then For grown-ups, and taps Get a code.

cancel.a: Yes, anytime. The plan runs to the end of the period you paid for, then your children go back to the free messages. Nothing they made is deleted.

store.q: What do you keep about me?
store.a: Your account name, a scrambled (hashed) password and which children are linked. We don't ask for your email. When you pay, Stripe handles the payment and keeps your email for receipts: we never see card numbers.

see.q: What can I see about my child?
see.a: Their name, and how many of the family's extra messages they used up to yesterday. Never their chats, friends, games, school or what they are doing right now.

reset.q: When do the free messages reset?

consent.q: Is linking or paying a form of parental consent?
consent.a: No. Linking and family plans are only about extra Builder messages. They are not how the site asks for or records consent.

faq.q1: Is Oomba Academy free for teachers?
faq.a1: Yes. Playing, classes, lessons and progress are free, and every student account gets free Builder messages each day.
faq.q2: Do students need an account or an email address to play?
faq.a2: No. Anyone can play straight away. For your classes you can make school accounts without any email address and print login cards for them.
faq.q3: Does it work on Chromebooks and school networks?
faq.a3: It runs in any up-to-date web browser, on Chromebooks, laptops, tablets and on the classroom board, with nothing to install. If your school filters websites, ask your IT team to allow {host}.
faq.q4: How do you protect student privacy?
faq.a4: We never ask students for an email address, age or home address. There are no ads and no tracking cookies, and a student's real name is seen only by their school's staff. Our privacy notice lists exactly what we keep.
faq.q5: What ages and grades is it for?
faq.a5: Oomba Academy is made for kindergarten to grade 8, about ages 5 to 14. Games such as Shark Plank and the first Sum Racer tracks suit the youngest players. Number Quest, the math course, runs from kindergarten to grade 8, and CS Quest and Cyber Defenders start in grade 3.
faq.q6: How do I add my class?
faq.a6: First, email us to set up your school. Then create a class and share its class code with students who have their own account, or make school accounts for the whole class and print login cards.
faq.a6google: First, email us to set up your school. Then create a class and share its class code with students who have their own account, or make school accounts for the whole class and print login cards. Schools that use Google can let students sign in with Google.
faq.q7: Can students make their own games? Who sees them?
faq.a7: Yes. A new game is private to the student who made it. They can share it with their class, and a game for everyone is reviewed before anyone else can play it.
faq.q8: Can I track progress and scores?
faq.a8: Yes. Lessons record each student’s progress, game scores and written answers. You see them on the class’s Progress tab, and can download each student’s lesson progress as a spreadsheet (CSV).
faq.a9: {count} languages, including Spanish, Portuguese, French, German, Arabic, Hebrew and Japanese. Each student picks their own.
faq.a4google: Students never type an email address, and we never ask for their age or home address. If your school uses Sign in with Google, we keep each student’s school Google email only to recognize their account. There are no ads and no tracking cookies. Our privacy notice lists exactly what we keep.

faq.a1paid: Playing, classes, lessons, progress and Oomba Live are free, and every student gets free Builder messages each day. The optional Teacher plan adds a shared daily pool of AI builds for your classes, with unlimited students. Try it free for 14 days, no card needed. Prices are on the plans page.

cs.title: CS Quest: computer science lessons for grades 3-8
cs.description: CS Quest is a free computer science program for grades 3-8: 23 lessons of 45 minutes in seven units, four games, live warm-ups and exit tickets, aligned to the CSTA K-12 standards.
cs.h1: CS Quest: computer science you can teach tomorrow
cs.lead: A full program for grades 3-8 that a teacher with no computer science background can run: every lesson is one 45-minute period with a plan, a game chapter, a live warm-up and an exit ticket.

badges.note: Why the counts differ: the 23 lessons include Unit 7, Make Your Own Game (four lessons in the AI Builder), which is not part of the student course map. The student map shows Units 1 to 6, plus a welcome step (0.1) and the Spark finale (6.4): 21 steps for grades 3-5, and 22 for grades 6-8, whose Unit 3 adds one practice step (3.4, Fair Data) with no classroom lesson of its own.

promise.li1: A plan for every period: Do Now, a projector script (say this, do this, ask this), the game chapter, discussion and an exit ticket.
promise.li2: Every lesson in two bands: Explorer for grades 3-5 and Pro for grades 6-8.
promise.li3: Warm-ups and exit tickets you can host live with a join code, or show on the projector one question at a time.
promise.li4: One click adds a lesson, a unit or a whole path to your library as your own copy to edit.
promise.li5: Assign a unit with a start date and a pace: every school day, twice a week or weekly.
promise.li6: An unplugged twin for every lesson, a sub plan and printables: cards, mats, tally sheets and half-sheet exit tickets.
promise.li7: A short-period (40 minute) version and a block (80-90 minute) version on every plan.
promise.li8: A coverage map and a Standards tab per class: practiced, checked and applied, per standard.

crew.p: Each game is a chapter book: one chapter per lesson, and the first level of every chapter is always open.
crew.roboRoute: Block coding: sequences, loops, conditionals, events, variables and functions, with a Level Maker.
crew.dataDetective: Collect, sort, chart and clean data, then pin only the claims the evidence supports.
crew.packetPost: Packets, routing and protocols, strong passphrases, spotting tricks and simple ciphers.
crew.insideTheMachine: Computer parts, hardware and software, troubleshooting, bits and pixels, and designing for everyone.

units.p: The units and their lessons, with the CSTA standards each one teaches.

paths.p: Pick a path, or teach the units in order. Core 10 needs no Builder and no school plan.

period.p: Every lesson follows the same shape, so students know what comes next.
period.short: Short periods drop to two warm-up items and one discussion prompt; the exit ticket is never cut.

claim.withH: With quiz steps and rubric marks on
claim.with: Every student practiced 1B-AP-10 in three lessons; the class averaged 71% on the nine unit 1 items tagged 1B-AP-10; 24 of 26 reached four of five checks in Loops.
claim.dayOne: Every student played the Loops lesson, with their best result, and the class's live results per question.
claim.note: The program page tells you which of the two your school gets. Practiced means a student finished the step, not mastery.

standards.p: Every lesson lists the CSTA K-12 Computer Science Standards (2017) it teaches; every level 1B and level 2 standard is the main focus of at least one lesson and is checked by at least one question. The unit 7 capstone rubric claims program-development and impacts standards only.

materials.p: One device per pair is enough. Every lesson has an unplugged twin for days without devices.

faq.q1: Do I need a computer science background?
faq.a1: No. Every plan has a projector script with what to say, what to do and what to ask, the misconception of the day and the big idea.
faq.q2: Do lessons need a school?
faq.a2: Yes. Classes and lessons live inside a school on Oomba Academy; set one up for free (one teacher is enough).
faq.a3: Any device with a modern browser, including Chromebooks without touch: everything is click-or-tap plus keyboard. One device per pair is enough.
faq.a4: 45 minutes. Every plan also has a 40-minute version and an 80-90 minute block version.
faq.a5: The CSTA K-12 Computer Science Standards (2017), levels 1B (grades 3-5) and 2 (grades 6-8). The coverage map shows each standard with its lessons, game chapters, questions and rubric lines.
faq.a6: Headphones are recommended. Lesson mode starts with music off and captions on.
faq.a7: Unit 7, where teams design and build a game with the Builder, needs a school plan. Every other unit works without it, and the Core 10 path skips it.
faq.a8: Students sign in with class login cards. They never type their full name into a game, and nothing they make is public unless you share it.
faq.a9: Yes. Adding a lesson gives you your own copy to edit. If CS Quest updates a lesson, you can reset to the new version; the old copy keeps your students' work.

start.staff: Open CS Quest and add the Core 10 path to your library.

cd.title: Cyber Defenders: cybersecurity lessons for grades 3-8
cd.description: Cyber Defenders is a free cybersecurity and online-safety course for grades 3-8: 20 short steps in two bands, played through Packet Post, Would You Rather, Trick Inbox and an escape-room finale, mapped to CYBER.ORG v1.0 and Common Sense Education.
cd.h1: Cyber Defenders: online safety you can teach tomorrow
cd.lead: A short course about how messages travel, how keys and codes protect them, what stays private, and how to spot a trick. Students join Pim the owl at the Netville post office, play real game missions, and earn a Defender stamp for every unit.

badges.units: An intro, 6 units and a finale

promise.li1: One story all the way through: Pim's post office, a magpie who slips fake letters into the post, and a stamp to earn in every unit.
promise.li2: Every step in two bands: Explorer for grades 3-5 and Pro for grades 6-8, with Pro wording and harder questions.
promise.li3: Short reading decks with real screenshots from the games, then a three-question check, then the game mission itself.
promise.li4: A step only counts as finished when the student has read the deck, passed the check and actually completed the game chapter. Opening the game is not enough.
promise.li5: The full standards map on this page: every step mapped to CYBER.ORG v1.0 and a Common Sense Education topic, ready to show a department head or a data-protection officer.
promise.li6: A teacher note for every unit: what to say first, what to watch for, and the lines that keep the hard topics calm.

crew.p: Packet Post is the post-office game the story lives in. Would You Rather carries the judgement calls, where there are no right answers and the learning is in the talking afterwards. Trick Inbox and the escape room join them in the second half of the course.
crew.packetPost: Deliver packets across Netville: how messages travel, what a seal promises, strong passphrases built by tapping word tiles, simple ciphers, and spotting trick messages.
crew.wouldYouRather: Short dilemmas about sharing, photos, footprints and credit. The Online: share or keep set carries units 3, 5 and 6.
crew.trickInbox: Sort a pretend inbox planted by the Magpie: hunt each message's hidden clues, then choose the move — deliver it, bin it, show Pim, or report and block. Its boss round is the incident drill in step 6.3.
crew.escape: Escape the Post Office: the escape-room finale. The Magpie locks the sorting room with six trick locks, one per unit, and the class's six Defender stamps are the key set. No fail state, no outcome-changing timer.

units.h: The intro, six units and the finale
units.p: Twenty steps in each band, in order. When the Pro title differs from the Explorer one, it is shown after it.

map.p: Every step, mapped. CYBER.ORG codes are shown per band; each step also carries its Common Sense Education topic, and an inherited CSTA code where the step re-frames a CS Quest lesson.
map.v1: This map is published on CYBER.ORG K-12 Cybersecurity Learning Standards v1.0 (August 2021). CYBER.ORG has since released a Version 2.0 (the National K-12 Cybersecurity and AI Learning Standards, September 2026); this course has not been re-mapped to it, and this page will say so plainly if that changes.
map.rename: Common Sense Education's newer Digital Literacy & Well-Being Curriculum renames the same six areas: Healthy Habits; Privacy & Safety; Digital Footprint; Relationships & Communication; Cyberbullying & Online Harm; Information & Media Literacy. The map uses the classic six names; each matches the new name in the same order.

notes.p: One short note per unit, written to print: say this first, watch for this. The same notes print with the standards map.

safety.li1: Children never type a real password, passphrase or account detail anywhere in the course. All key practice happens inside Packet Post, with a pretend mailbox key built by tapping tiles.
safety.li2: No step asks a child to open, check or change a real account as homework. Every example is fictional: no real brands, people, schools or addresses.
safety.li3: The course collects nothing new. Progress and checks use the same kid-safe machinery as the rest of Oomba Academy: no chat, no ads, no third parties.
safety.li4: The Magpie is a comic bird, never a person, and every trick is shown after the fact with its clues named. The aim is clue-spotting, never fear.

finale.h: The finale: Escape the Post Office
finale.p: The course ends in an escape room. On Spark Day the Magpie locks the sorting room with six trick locks, one for each unit, and the six Defender stamps the class has earned are the keys — each stamp proves the skill its lock tests. Students read the room first, match every lock to the unit that trained them for it, then open the locks in any order.
finale.li1: Sorting Gate — routing: send the golden letter along the right roads (Unit 1).
finale.li2: Sealed Note — the cipher wheel: unscramble a sealed message (Unit 2).
finale.li3: Which Pim? — footprint clues: pick the real Pim from the trails each one left (Unit 3).
finale.li4: Trick Inbox — a round of trick-spotting under pressure (Unit 4).
finale.li5: Five Moves — the incident drill, in the right order (the Kind Screen stamp, Unit 5; drilled in step 6.3).
finale.li6: Layers — defense in depth: match each layer of protection to what it stops (Unit 6).
finale.fair: The room keeps fair rules: there is no fail state and no timer that can change the outcome. Three hint feathers are there to be used, and the completion shield says honestly how many were used. In Pro, the parade clock only changes the celebration, never the result, and the locks are cut harder — a spoofed sender to catch, defense spelled the US way.

print.p: Two printed packs. The standards map and the teacher notes: one map to file with your planning, and one short note per unit to read before the lesson. And the Spot-the-Trick pack: 18 printable message cards — the Trick Inbox game's own messages, tricks and safe ones mixed — with a teacher answer key naming each card's clues and right move. Print the cards for an offline lesson, a classroom wall, or a class with no devices that day.

faq.q1: Do I need a cybersecurity background?
faq.a1: No. Each step teaches its own idea in plain words before the game, and the teacher note for the unit tells you what to say first and what to watch for.
faq.q2: Does it need a school account?
faq.a2: No. Cyber Defenders stands alone: no CS Quest knowledge and no school setup needed. Students open the course, pick the Explorer or Pro band, and start; signing in just keeps their progress.
faq.q3: How long does a step take?
faq.a3: About 15 minutes: a short deck, a three-question check, and one game chapter. The intro, the six units and the finale make 20 steps per band, so the whole course fits in about five hours, or one step a week across two terms.
faq.a4: CYBER.ORG K-12 Cybersecurity Learning Standards v1.0 for grades 3-5 and 6-8, with each step also tagged to a Common Sense Education digital citizenship topic. The full map is on this page.
faq.a5: Yes: free for classrooms, with no ads and nothing to install. It runs in the browser on any device, including Chromebooks.
faq.a6: Step 6.4, Escape the Post Office: the Magpie locks the sorting room with six trick locks, one per unit, and the class's six stamps are the keys. There is no fail state and no timer that can change the outcome; three hint feathers are there to be used, and the completion shield says how many were used.
