geoboard.pickTri: {i, plural, one {# peg} other {# pegs}} inside, {b} on the band: 2 × {i} + {b} − 2 = {a} triangles
geoboard.radiusOne: Measured with the circle's radius as 1 unit.
geoboard.open: Close the band to see its area.
geoboard.crosses: The band crosses itself, so it has no single area. Undo a peg.
geoboard.hint: Tap pegs to stretch a band; tap the first peg again to close it. Drag a corner to move it.
geoboard.empty: Tap pegs to make a band.
geoboard.pickOne: Tap a band to measure it.
geoboard.noRoom: That's the most there can be. Delete one first.
geoboard.modeText: Text: tap where the label goes
geoboard.modeErase: Eraser: tap or rub out a drawing
geoboard.inkFull: That's the most drawings. Rub some out first.
geoboard.local: Your drawings and labels stay on this screen.
geoboard.resetDone: Board cleared. Undo brings it back.
geoboard.title: Challenge
geoboard.titlePh: Type a challenge for the class…
geoboard.idea1: Make a shape with an area of 12 square units.
geoboard.idea2: How many different shapes with an area of 12 can you make?
geoboard.idea3: Make a triangle with an area of 6 square units.
geoboard.idea4: Make two shapes with the same area but different perimeters.
geoboard.idea5: Make a shape with exactly two right angles.
geoboard.howto: Tap pegs to stretch a band. Tap the first peg again to close it.
geoboard.helpUse:
Tap pegs to stretch a band; tap the first peg to close it.
Drag a corner or a whole band. A color starts a new band.
Shapes, Tools and Annotate add shapes, a ruler, labels and a pen.
geoboard.helpIdeas: Try: everyone makes an area of 12, then compares perimeters.

pattern.name: Geometry
pattern.desc: Pattern blocks, 3D shapes that fold into nets, and slides, flips and turns on a grid.
pattern.notHex: Squares and thin rhombi ({n}) are not fractions of the hexagon.
pattern.hint: Drag blocks; they snap to the grid.
pattern.empty: Add a block from the row above. Arrow keys move the chosen block and R turns it.
pattern.howto: Tap a block above to add it. Drag blocks; they snap together.
pattern.helpUse:
Tap a placed block to choose it, then Turn or Remove.
The readout is the fraction of a hexagon the blocks make.
Arrow keys move the chosen block; R turns it.
pattern.helpIdeas: How many ways can you cover a hexagon?

angle.name: Angle maker
angle.desc: Two rays and a protractor. The angle in degrees and its name. Grades 4–8.
angle.hint: Drag the end of the ray, or use the arrow keys.
angle.howto: Drag the end of the ray, or use − and + to change the angle.
angle.helpUse:
Jump to… picks 45°, 90°, 135°, 180° or 270°.
The size and the name of the angle are shown below.
Protractor and Arc switch each on or off; Options sets the snap.
angle.helpIdeas: Hide the protractor and ask for an estimate first.

solids.name: 3D shapes and nets
solids.desc: Cubes, prisms, pyramids, cylinders and cones that fold and unfold. Count faces, edges and vertices. Grades 1–8.
solids.view: Fold it: arrow keys. Turn it: Page Up and Page Down.
solids.howto: Pick a shape. Fold or unfold it; drag sideways to turn it.
solids.helpUse:
The second menu marks the faces, edges or vertices.
Turn also turns it; faces, edges and vertices are counted below.
Arrow keys fold it; Page Up and Page Down turn it.
solids.helpIdeas: Show a flat net and ask which solid it makes before you fold it.

transform.name: Transformations
transform.desc: Slide, flip and turn a shape on a grid, with its starting place and every point's coordinates. Grades 4–8.
transform.offGrid: Part of the shape has moved off the grid.
transform.hint: Arrow keys or a drag slide the shape.
transform.howto: Pick slide, flip or turn. Drag the shape or use the controls.
transform.helpUse:
Translate: − and + on x and y slide the shape.
Reflect and Rotate: the menu picks the mirror line or turn.
The rule and each point before and after are shown.
transform.helpIdeas: Rotate 90° and ask where point A will land before you show it.

balance.name: Balance scale
balance.desc: Solve equations with x-boxes and weights: do the same to both sides and it stays level. Grades 3 and up.
balance.div: Share each side into {n} equal groups and keep one
balance.tipsL: It tips: the left side is heavier.
balance.tipsR: It tips: the right side is heavier.
balance.level: Level: both sides weigh the same.
balance.cant: That can't be done to this side.
balance.howto: Drag tiles onto a pan, or onto Both sides. Keep it level; find x.
balance.helpUse:
Drag tiles onto a pan, or off it to take them away.
One side only: it tips. Both sides: it stays level.
Try x =, then Check: do both sides weigh the same?
balance.helpIdeas: Solve 3x + 5 = 2x + 10: take an x from both sides first.
balance.tray: Tiles: drag one onto the scale
balance.sign: New tiles are {s}. Press to switch + and −.
balance.bothHint: Drop a tile here: the same to both
balance.zeroed: {n, plural, one {# zero pair} other {# zero pairs}} removed
balance.pickFirst: Pick a tile first (tap one), then tap Both sides.
balance.picked: {t} picked: now tap where it goes.
balance.full: There is no room for that tile.

algebra.name: Algebra
algebra.desc: Algebra tiles with zero pairs, and a balance scale to solve equations step by step.
algebra.pairs: {n, plural, one {# zero pair} other {# zero pairs}}
algebra.hint: No zero pairs left: this is as simple as it gets.
algebra.empty: Drag tiles here from the tray.
algebra.howto: Drag tiles onto the mat. Drop a tile on its opposite to make 0.
algebra.helpUse:
Drag tiles onto the mat, or off it to take them away.
A dashed box is a zero pair: together they make 0.
Challenge gives you an expression to build, then Check.
algebra.helpIdeas: Build 2x + 3 − x − 1, then simplify it with zero pairs.
algebra.tray: Tiles: drag or tap one to put it on the mat
algebra.sign: New tiles are {s}. Press to switch + and −.
algebra.notPair: Only a tile and its opposite make 0 (like +x and −x).
algebra.legend: a dashed box is a zero pair. Drag one tile onto the other.
algebra.picked: {t} picked: tap its opposite to make 0, or Flip sign.
algebra.selHint: {t} picked: tap its opposite to make 0, Flip sign, or Delete.
algebra.pickTile: Tap a tile on the mat first.

coins.name: Coins and money
coins.desc: Count coins and notes, see the total, and make change. Simple drawn coins, never real pictures. Grades K–4.
coins.countUp: Count up from what it costs, smallest coins first.
coins.fewest: The fewest coins and notes for this: {n}
coins.empty: Tap a coin or note above to put it here.
coins.units: Amounts here are in cents or pence (plain numbers for the plain set).
coins.howto: Tap coins and notes above to add them. Tap a pile to take one.
coins.helpUse:
Count adds up the money; Make change works out the change.
In Make change, − and + set the cost and what was paid.
Options: which money. Clear empties the mat.
coins.helpIdeas: It costs 37, paid with 100: count up together to find the change.

chance.name: Data and chance
chance.desc: Bar, line, picture and dot graphs, and a chance lab: coins, dice and spinners up to 1,000 times.
chance.hint: The dashed line on each bar is how many we expect.
chance.howto: Pick coin, dice or spinner, then Run. Compare with the dashed line.
chance.helpUse:
The menu sets how many trials each Run does.
Start again clears the results.
Options: one die or two, the spinner's parts, up to 1000 trials.
chance.helpIdeas: Predict, run 10 tosses, then 1000: which is closer to half?

letters.name: Letter tiles
letters.desc: Build words from letter tiles, vowels marked, with word families (-at, -ig, -ake...). Nobody types. Grades K–3.

letters.hint: Tap or drag letters to build a word.

terms.title: Reusing your figures
terms.lead: Every figure you make in Figures is free for you to use. Here is what that means, in plain words.
terms.can1: Use your figures in class, on worksheets and tests, in slides and on websites.
terms.can2: Copy, print and share them with anyone: students, families and other teachers.
terms.can3: Change them: crop them, add labels, or build them into your own materials.
terms.can4: Use them in materials you publish or sell.
terms.can5: Do all of this without asking us and without giving credit. A mention is welcome, never required.
terms.noticeText: Every SVG or PNG you download or copy carries this note, written into the file itself, where image programs and search engines look for it. It is in English so it reads the same everywhere:
terms.noticeMeans: It means Oomba Academy gives up any rights it has in its part of the figure (the drawing, the layout and the labels it makes), so anyone may reuse that part. You may keep the note or take it out.
terms.cc0Text: CC0 1.0 is a public domain dedication from Creative Commons. For our part of a figure there are no conditions at all: no credit, no license to follow, anywhere in the world, as far as the law allows.
terms.cc0Link: Read CC0 1.0 on the Creative Commons website
terms.yoursText: Anything original you add is yours: your own question, your own labels and data, and your own drawings. Whether others may reuse those parts is up to you.
terms.care1: Check a figure before you use it. We check figures carefully, but we cannot promise that every figure is right for every use.
terms.care2: Keep students' names and personal details out of figures you share.
terms.care3: These terms are about the figures you export. The rest of Oomba Academy follows the site's own terms.

settings.title: Oomba, the teaching companion
settings.text: Teachers with the Teacher plan can ask Oomba for games, books, dashboard changes and lesson help from a bubble on their pages. Students never see it. Their messages, attached text and pictures go to our AI provider, Anthropic, with students' names taken out.
settings.onHint: Off: no Oomba bubble for any teacher in this school.
settings.webHint: On: Oomba may search the web for teaching questions and shows its sources. Searches never include names.
